# Saved ship configurations: re-purchase and equip a known build in one action

## Problem statement

When a hex battle ends, the deployed ship is consumed (AH-0MWL5PAP2001XYYF) and the player must rebuild from salvage, so re-purchasing and re-equipping a known build is repeated busywork. Saved ship configurations let the player store a named build once and re-apply it — purchase plus equip every part — in a single action, then fly.

## Users

- **Primary — the player** who repeatedly flies the same preferred build through the hex war and re-fits it after each sortie.
- **Secondary — the balance/progression owner**, because reducing re-fit friction makes the post-battle economy treadmill tolerable.

Example user stories:

- As a player, I want to save my preferred build by name, so I don't have to remember which hull, weapons and modifiers I fly.
- As a player, I want to select a saved build from a drop-down and have every part purchased and equipped in one action, so re-fitting after a battle takes one click instead of a dozen.
- As a player, I want a saved build I cannot currently afford to tell me exactly what is missing (which entries/minerals/cores), so I know what to earn before I try again.
- As a player, I want to rename or delete saved builds, so the list stays useful as my builds evolve.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Save a named build.** The hangar can capture the currently equipped ship configuration as a named saved build: the equipped hull (`activeHull`), the equipped starting weapons (`activeLoadout.startingWeapons`), the equipped modifiers (`activeLoadout.modifiers`), and the permanent levels that configuration relies on (`hangar.weaponLevels` / `hangar.powerUpLevels` rows for those kinds).
- **One-action purchase and equip.** A drop-down on the hangar screen lists saved builds; selecting one **purchases and equips every upgrade the build needs in one action** — the hull becomes `activeHull`, starting weapons join `activeLoadout.startingWeapons`, modifiers join `activeLoadout.modifiers`, and any missing permanent levels are bought — through the existing pure economy/payload updaters, never scene-only logic.
- **Affordable builds apply atomically; unaffordable builds report the shortfall.** A build whose combined salvage cost the player cannot currently afford must report the exact shortfall (which entries, minerals and/or cores are missing) and apply **nothing** — neither partial purchase nor partial equip, and no currency spent.
- **Saved builds can be saved, renamed and deleted.** The hangar surface supports creating a saved build from the current configuration, renaming an existing one, and deleting one, and the list is persisted in the hangar-war payload. **Saved builds survive a war reset** (producer decision): `restartHangarWar` preserves the saved-build list alongside `bestScore`, because saved configurations are a "what you own" meta-layer rather than war progress.
- **Saved builds are unbounded in number, with a delete affordance.** There is no cap on how many saved builds a player may hold (producer decision), so the drop-down list plus the save/rename/delete surface is the only management mechanism — deleting a build must be reachable for every entry.
- **A saved build referencing a now-unavailable entry never breaks.** Selecting a saved build whose parts are not in the catalogue (or are ring-gated) reports the same shortfall/refusal path rather than throwing or silently applying a partial build; the economy's `owned → gated → unaffordable` precedence is respected.
- **Automated tests cover the feature through the pure core and the scene seam (gym↔game parity).** Saving captures the exact equipped set plus level rows; selecting an affordable build purchases and equips atomically; an unaffordable build reports every missing item/currency and applies nothing; rename/delete round-trip (deletion reachable for every saved build); a saved build missing a catalogue entry refuses safely; `restartHangarWar` keeps the saved-build list while wiping unlocks/levels/loadout; and the payload round-trips through `hangarWarStore` without a schema-version bump (the shape is additive).
- **All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes**, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Impact

After a battle you pick your saved build from the hangar drop-down and, if you can afford it, the whole ship is re-purchased and re-equipped in one action — re-fitting becomes one click instead of repeated busywork.

## Constraints

- **Pure core, scene seam.** Purchase, equip and level arithmetic live in the pure economy/payload updaters; the screen and scene only present and persist, so gym↔game parity holds (`docs/GYM_PARITY.md`).
- **Atomic apply.** A build applies fully or not at all; no partial purchase, no partial equip, no spend on a refused build.
- **Additive payload field.** Saved builds are a new optional field on the hangar payload, migrated by field presence without a schema-version bump (the established pattern for `weaponLevels` / `powerUpLevels` / `frontierTick`), and omitted on write when empty so a save round-trips byte-for-byte.
- **War-reset interaction.** `restartHangarWar` currently calls `createDefaultPayload`, which resets the entire hangar to starters (all unlocks, levels and loadout). The producer decided **saved builds survive a reset**, so `restartHangarWar` must thread `savedBuilds` through beside `bestScore` (other hangar state stays at the reset default).
- **One payload write.** Applying a build persists through the existing `saveHangarWarPayload`; demo/attract runs must never overwrite the player's war (existing demo guard).
- **No soft-lock.** A saved build must never leave the player with no deployable ship; the free starter hull/weapon rules are unchanged.
- **Economy precedence preserved.** A build's parts are validated with the existing `owned → gated → unaffordable` rule; auto-enable on purchase (AH-0MWL9EC3L002GKYR) is the per-part primitive this feature composes, not a re-implementation.
- **Scope creep risk.** A full loadout-preset/sharing system, cross-device sync, or balance tuning of prices is out of scope; record extra opportunities as linked work items rather than expanding this one.

## Existing state

- `HangarState` (`src/core/hangarWar/types.ts`) holds `activeHull`, `activeLoadout` (starting weapons + modifiers), `unlockedHulls`/`unlockedWeapons`/`ownedModifiers`, and optional `weaponLevels`/`powerUpLevels` rows; it has **no** saved-build field.
- `hangarEconomy.ts` owns the pure purchase rules (`buy`, `canBuy`, `costToUpgrade`, `buyUpgrade`, `equipHull`, `equipLoadout`, `resolveActiveLoadout`) and the `owned → gated → unaffordable` precedence.
- `hangarScreen.ts` exposes pure payload updaters (`purchaseHangarEntry`, `upgradeHangarKind`, `equipHangarHull`, `toggleHangarWeapon`, `restartHangarWar`) and the shared `buildHangarScreenModel`/`renderHangarScreen` used by both `HangarScene` and `GymHangar`.
- `hangarWarStore.ts` parses/normalises the payload (additive fields migrated by presence) and `createDefaultPayload` seeds the starter kit.
- AH-0MWL9EC3L002GKYR (auto-enable a purchase in the hangar) is the per-part "buying arms it immediately" primitive this feature builds on; AH-0MWL5PAP2001XYYF is the parent consumption work.

## Desired change

- Add a saved-build contract (name + hull + starting weapons + modifiers + the permanent level rows the build relies on) and an additive `savedBuilds` field on `HangarState`/the payload, parsed and normalised like the other additive fields.
- Add pure helpers to capture the current configuration as a build, and a pure "apply a saved build" reducer that validates affordability and atomically purchases + equips every part (reusing `buy` with `equipOnPurchase` and the level-upgrade path), returning either the new payload or a structured shortfall.
- Surface a drop-down list plus save/rename/delete affordances on the hangar screen, with the unaffordable shortfall rendered like the existing refused-purchase messaging.
- Persist through the single `saveHangarWarPayload` write; confirm the payload round-trips without a schema bump.
- Preserve the saved-build list across `restartHangarWar` (thread `savedBuilds` through beside `bestScore`).

## Risks & assumptions

- **War-reset boundary (resolved).** `restartHangarWar` resets the whole hangar to starters; the producer decided saved builds survive, so thread `savedBuilds` through `restartHangarWar` beside `bestScore`. Test that a reset keeps the saved-build list while wiping unlocks/levels/loadout.
- **Partial-application bugs.** Applying a build touches ownership, loadout and level rows at once. Mitigation: one pure reducer that either returns a complete new payload or a structured shortfall, with a test asserting no currency is spent on refusal.
- **Stale builds.** A saved build may name a ring-gated or removed catalogue entry after a war reset or catalogue change. Mitigation: validate through the economy's `owned → gated → unaffordable` precedence and report the shortfall rather than partially applying.
- **Atomicity vs auto-enable.** AH-0MWL9EC3L002GKYR auto-enables a *single* purchase; a build is many purchases that must land atomically. Mitigation: compose the per-part primitive inside the build reducer, not the screen.
- **UI list growth.** Saved builds are unbounded by producer decision. Mitigation: the delete affordance keeps the list manageable; render the drop-down with scrolling if it overflows the screen.
- **Scope creep.** A general loadout-preset/sharing system or price/balance tuning could creep in. Mitigation: record extra opportunities as linked work items; keep this item to save/apply/rename/delete + shortfall.
- **Assumptions:** saved builds capture equipped ids plus the level rows they rely on; applying a build validates all parts before spending; demo/attract runs never persist a build application (existing demo guard).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/core/hangarWar/types.ts` — add `SavedShipBuild` and the additive `savedBuilds?` field on `HangarState`.
- `src/core/hangarWar/hangarEconomy.ts` — pure `buildFromHangar`, `applySavedBuild` (atomic purchase+equip, structured shortfall), reusing `buy`/`buyUpgrade`.
- `src/core/hangarWar/hangarWarStore.ts` — parse/normalise `savedBuilds` by field presence (no version bump), omit when empty.
- `src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarScreen.ts` — pure `saveBuild`/`renameBuild`/`deleteBuild`/`selectBuild` updaters plus screen model rows for the drop-down and management actions; `restartHangarWar` preserves `savedBuilds`.
- `src/scenes/HangarScene.ts` — wire the updaters and the single persist.
- Tests beside each module plus the `hangarWarFlow` integration test and the gym parity scene.

## Related work

- **AH-0MWL5PAP2001XYYF** — Completing a hex battle means the equipped hulls/weapons/plugins are reset (parent; defines the consumption this feature re-fits after).
- **AH-0MWL9EC3L002GKYR** — Auto-enable a purchase in the hangar (the per-part buy-and-arm primitive this feature composes).
- **AH-0MVUXC1GQ00366Z6** — Hangar economy and unlock tree (the purchase/equip rules).
- **AH-0MVUXC1X6007KAG1** — Hangar screen shared model/renderer (the surface this extends).
- **AH-0MVZJ6V1J001DA9D** — Empty-loadout legality (must be preserved).
- Docs: `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` (Candidate D persistence rules), `docs/GYM_PARITY.md`.

### Related work (automated report)

- **AH-0MT9FRVF00086TO3** – Ship configuration file: load and save values (completed) — a *run-time* ship-stat config file, not the hangar economy; related by name only.
- **AH-0MT9FS3DL0084Z6V** – Gym scene: ship config sliders, save button, half-speed ship (completed) — run-time gym ship config; related by name only.
- **AH-0MUFE1N36007X48T** – Set Asteroids as the default ship control scheme and accept headerless CSV seed format (completed) — unrelated (control scheme / seed format).
- **Repository matches:** `docs/Game Design Document.md`, `README.md`, `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md`.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Should a saved build capture permanent levels too, not just the equipped ids?" — Answer (seed context, AH-0MWL5PAP2001XYYF Q1 follow-on): yes — the build includes "the permanent levels the build relies on", so re-applying it buys the levels as well as the parts. Source: parent item description and producer's Q1 follow-on (save ship configurations, select to quickly purchase the needed upgrades).
- Q: "What should happen when the player cannot afford every part of a saved build?" — Answer (seed context, this item): report the shortfall (which entries/minerals/cores are missing) rather than partially applying or silently failing — apply nothing. Source: item description; consistent with the economy's refused-purchase contract.
- Q: "Do saved builds survive a war reset (RESTART WAR / `restartHangarWar`)?" — Answer (producer): **yes** — saved builds survive a war reset; `restartHangarWar` preserves the saved-build list alongside `bestScore`. Source: interactive reply (producer Q1 = yes), 2026-11-17.
- Q: "Is the drop-down on the existing hangar screen, or a new surface?" — Answer: on the existing hangar screen (`buildHangarScreenModel`/`renderHangarScreen`), so gym parity is automatic. Source: this item description ("A drop-down on the hangar screen"); AH-0MVUXC1X6007KAG1.
- Q: "Should saved builds be scoped/limited (max count)?" — Answer (producer): **unbounded**, but provide a way to delete them. Source: interactive reply (producer Q2), 2026-11-17.

## Traceability

- Duplicate check performed — searched `saved build configuration hangar`; no existing item covers saved ship configurations. Closest items are the parent consumption work (AH-0MWL5PAP2001XYYF), the auto-enable primitive (AH-0MWL9EC3L002GKYR) and the economy/screen items listed above, which this item composes rather than duplicates.
data.title: Saved ship configurations: re-purchase and equip a known build in one action

# Reconcile arena moving-hostile profiles with the class models and fix the chaser over-dodge

**Raised by:** AH-0MWM0C5BN003PCDT (seeded per-class avoidance sweep).
**Blocks:** AH-0MWM0C5BN003PCDT — the sweep cannot satisfy its pass bar until this lands.
**Priority:** high (epic AH-0MWLUIOH9001XBJ3 acceptance evidence).

## Problem

The seeded per-class sweep over the headless arena (Feature 6's moving-hostile
opt-in, live competent brain, `hazardMotionModelEnabled` on/off, 12 seeds,
1800 ticks, 4 immortal single-class bodies, 2 minerals) measures **avoidable**
enemy-body contacts (a contact is avoidable when a 16-direction escape fan at
`playerSpeed` clears the contact radius from the body's fitted velocity 0.25 s
before the overlap). Measured with the arena's shipped class profiles:

| class | contacts off | contacts on | seeds better / worse / tie | aggregate off→on |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| chaser | 46 | 39 | 5 / 0 / 7 | −15% |
| diver | 79 | 47 | 9 / 0 / 3 | −41% |
| patroller | 19 | 21 | 4 / 4 / 4 | +11% |
| formation (control) | 10 | 26 | 1 / 5 / 6 | +160% |
| roamer (control) | 22 | 20 | 2 / 1 / 9 | −9% |

The AC's bar (curving classes strictly fewer on a **majority** of seeds;
`roamer`/`formation` **never increase**) is therefore not met: `chaser` reduces
but only on 5/12 seeds, `patroller` is flat, and both controls increase on some
seeds. The 60 Hz scripted-curving proof in
`src/ai/botSteering.integration.test.ts` (off: min distance 25.7 px, inside the
30 px contact radius; on: 39.2 px, clear) shows the model *does* work when the
scripted trajectory matches the class model — so the failure is in the harness /
live closed-loop interaction, not in the sampler's core idea.

## Diagnosis

1. **Harness and predictor disagree about the class semantics.** Feature 6's
   arena profiles are a sinusoidal `patroller` weave and a circular `formation`
   sway (`hostileMotionVelocity`), while the predictor's class models are
   `patroller` = straight patrol then straight commit and `formation` = linear
   drift + edge reflection (`src/ai/framework/hazardMotionModel.ts`). The sweep
   is validating each predictor against a trajectory it does not model.
   Re-running with the arena profile temporarily changed to the predictor's
   semantics made both classes neutral-to-better (patroller aggregate 58→51,
   89→81; formation 23→19, 13→12), confirming the mismatch.
2. **The chaser over-dodges.** With the model on, a pursuing chaser is predicted
   to threaten every bearing; `planSteering` picks the least-bad escape, which
   keeps the ship near the body, and rising-edge contacts increase (the control
   arm flies its line and often finishes with one contact per body). This is the
   behaviour the pinned note in `hazardMotionModel.test.ts` warned about.
3. **The metric is coarse.** With 4 immortal bodies, contacts saturate at one
   per body, so per-seed comparisons are dominated by ties. Any fix should
   either raise the encounter rate (fast crossing geometry) or measure at a
   finer granularity while keeping the AC's per-seed rule.

## Acceptance criteria

- The arena's moving-hostile class profiles and the predictor's class models
  describe the **same** trajectory semantics, asserted by a test (a class
  profile the predictor does not model must fail that test).
- The chaser sweep arm no longer regresses: a live competent bot with the
  motion model on records **no more** avoidable contacts than the
  constant-velocity control on any seed, and strictly fewer on a majority.
- The seeded per-class sweep (`src/ai/eval/hazardMotionSweep.test.ts`) lands
  green with the AC bar: `chaser`/`diver`/`patroller` strictly fewer avoidable
  contacts on a majority of a documented seed list; `roamer`/`formation` never
  increase. A failure names the offending seed and class.
- With that evidence, flip `COMPETENT_BOT_TUNABLES.hazardMotionModelEnabled` to
  `true`, update the pin in `hazardMotionModel.test.ts` (with the evidence
  reference, not silently), and re-baseline any eval expectation the flip
  genuinely moves, recording the rationale.

## Evidence / artefacts

- `src/ai/eval/arena.ts` — the moving mode now exposes each hostile's stable
  `id`/`movementClass` on the bot snapshot (only under the opt-in), which the
  tracker needs to fit a velocity at all.
- `src/ai/botSteering.integration.test.ts` — the 60 Hz scripted-curving proof.
- Measurement harness and per-seed numbers reproducible from the described
  scenario (recorded on AH-0MWM0C5BN003PCDT).

**Key files:** `src/ai/eval/arena.ts`, `src/ai/framework/hazardMotionModel.ts`,
`src/ai/framework/competent/steering.ts`, `src/ai/framework/competent/tunables.ts`,
`src/ai/eval/hazardMotionSweep.test.ts` (new), `src/ai/eval/arena.test.ts`.

# Intake Brief — Automatically select strong weapons (AH-0MWOROJYT004WPSD)

## Problem statement

The target-aware hangar (config) screen already shows the chosen hex boss's
intel and marks every weapon row `▲ EFFECTIVE` (green) / `▼ RESISTED` (red),
but the loadout itself is left entirely to the player: a fresh deployment
carries an **empty** starting-weapon selection, and a returning player may carry
a stale mix that ignores the upcoming boss, so the recorded intel does not
change what the fleet actually flies with. The ask is to make the screen choose
a sensible default — automatically equip the owned weapons that are **strong**
against the target boss, then fill the remaining loadout capacity with a
balanced variety of weapons/power-ups — and to colour the equipped list green
(strong) and red (weak). A fresh (empty) loadout is auto-fitted on open, and an
explicit **apply suggested buildout** button lets the player apply the
recommendation at any time.

## Users

- **Player arriving at a hex** — wants the strongest sensible kit selected for
  them so a hex battle does not begin under-equipped or with a stale loadout.
  - *As a player, when I open the hangar for a hex whose boss the Wave Laser
    counters, I want the Wave Laser already equipped, so I do not have to
    re-derive the intel myself.*
  - *As a player, I want the remaining slots filled with a varied, useful mix
    rather than one family stacked to the cap.*
- **Player who customises** — wants their deliberate choice to survive; the
  automatic fit applies to an empty (default) loadout only, and an explicit
  button applies the suggestion when *they* choose to.
- **Producer/designer** — wants one shared, pure selection rule consumed by the
  game and `GymHangar`, so no scene owns a second loadout policy and the
  gym↔game parity rule holds.
- **Maintainer** — wants the selection to reuse the shipped six-slot cap and
  the shipped matchup resolver (`resolveBossMatchup`) rather than introduce a
  second power/strength model.

## Existing state (verified in code)

- **Matchup display already exists.** `resolveBossMatchup(weaponId, definition)`
  (`src/core/hangarWar/weaponMatchup.ts`) returns `'strong' | 'weak' |
  'neutral'`; `buildHangarWeaponOptions` marks each weapon row with
  `withMatchupMarker` and `rowColour` applies `HANGAR_STRONG_COLOR` /
  `HANGAR_WEAK_COLOR` (`src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarScreen.ts`). The colouring
  part of the seed intent is **already satisfied for weapon rows**; only
  weapons carry a boss matchup, so power-up rows stay neutral.
- **The default loadout is deliberately empty.** GDD § *Hangar economy and
  unlock tree* and AH-0MVZJ6V1J001DA9D: `activeLoadout.startingWeapons: []`,
  and "owning the free starter weapon never auto-equips it — equipping a
  starter is always a deliberate choice". This item revises that default for the
  pre-battle case: an empty loadout is auto-fitted.
- **A purchase auto-equips.** `purchaseHangarEntry` buys with
  `equipOnPurchase: true`, so bought parts already land owned-and-armed. This
  is a different mechanism from the requested automatic selection.
- **Six shared loadout slots.** `POWER_UP_SLOT_CAP = 6`
  (`src/core/constants.ts`); weapons and power-ups share the cap.
  `applyHangarWarDeployment` (`src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarDeployment.ts`) trims
  the combined list (selected weapons first, then owned power-up levels)
  through `capDropIdsToSlotPool` before granting, so an over-full loadout is
  already trimmed silently — the screen can show more selected weapons than the
  run actually carries (AH-0MVVF0POV001JNKX).
- **Power-ups are not loadout-selectable today.** Every owned level-bearing
  power-up is granted on deployment (`levels.powerUps`); `HangarLoadout` has
  only `startingWeapons` and `modifiers`. Making power-ups installable is a
  **separate work item** (AH-0MWOV8SMI006W52Z, spawned by producer Q2 = A);
  this item budgets around the auto-granted power-ups.
- **Every deployment has a target hex.** The hangar screen accepts an optional
  `targetHexId` (set when the map opens it via `HexMapScene.openConfig`); with
  none, `selectDeploymentHex` still resolves the weakest unheld hex, so the
  screen almost always has a boss to fit against.
- **No auto-selection exists today.** There is no auto-fit function, no
  "the player customised this loadout" flag, and no variety rule for a > cap
  owned set.
- **Weapon behaviour families.** Weapons expose behaviour descriptors
  (`aoe`, `bounce`, `hitscan`, `splits`, `orbit`, plain projectiles) in
  `src/utils/weapons.ts`; the variety rule can key on these rather than invent
  a taxonomy.

## Desired change

1. Add a **pure auto-loadout selector** that, given the payload, the target hex
   definition and the catalogue, returns a starting-weapon selection under this
   rule (producer Q3 = "A then C"):
   - include every owned weapon whose matchup is `strong` against the boss;
   - never include a `weak` weapon by auto-selection;
   - enforce the **variety cap**: at most one weapon per behaviour family
     (spread / beam / bounce / split / orbit / AoE);
   - then prefer, in order: `strong`, at least one defensive power-up that the
     deployment will auto-grant, and the highest permanent level;
   - fill toward the shared six-slot cap, budgeting for the owned power-ups that
     will also consume slots at grant time, and never exceed the cap.
2. Apply the selector **automatically only when the loadout is at its default
   (empty) state** (producer Q1 = B), so a deliberate loadout is preserved.
3. Provide an explicit **apply suggested buildout** button that renders the
   suggested selection and applies it when the player activates it (producer Q1
   = B, explicit action). The button is available regardless of whether the
   current loadout is empty.
4. Keep the manual toggles working after auto-selection, and keep the six-slot
   display honest (the selected list should not claim more slots than the run
   will grant).
5. Preserve the equipped-list colours: strong rows green, weak rows red, always
   paired with a non-colour glyph tag (CVD policy); the gym renders the same
   model read-only (gym↔game parity).
6. Update the design-of-record wording (GDD § Hangar economy and unlock tree,
   `docs/GYM_PARITY.md`, module JSDoc) to state the auto-fit-when-empty rule,
   the apply-suggested-buildout button and the variety rule.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Strong weapons are auto-equipped when the loadout is empty.**
      Opening the hangar screen ahead of a battle with an empty loadout on a hex
      whose authored `weaknesses` name an owned weapon selects that weapon in
      `activeLoadout.startingWeapons` (via `resolveBossMatchup === 'strong'`);
      pinned by a pure selector test.
- [ ] **AC2 — Weak weapons are never auto-selected.** An owned weapon whose
      matchup is `weak` is never added by the auto-selector, and is not forced
      into the selection by the fill step.
- [ ] **AC3 — Variety then preference (Q3 = A then C).** The selector applies at
      most one weapon per behaviour family, then prefers `strong`, then at least
      one defensive power-up the deployment will auto-grant, then the highest
      permanent level, and fills toward the shared six-slot cap
      (`POWER_UP_SLOT_CAP`) without exceeding it — accounting for the owned
      power-ups that also consume slots at grant time.
- [ ] **AC4 — A deliberate loadout is preserved; the button applies it on
      demand.** Auto-fit runs only when the loadout is at its default (empty)
      state, so a hand-picked loadout is never silently overwritten; an explicit
      **apply suggested buildout** button renders the suggestion and applies it
      when activated, for any loadout.
- [ ] **AC5 — Manual control is preserved.** After auto-selection the player can
      still toggle any owned weapon.
- [ ] **AC6 — Equipped list colour semantics.** The equipped/loadout list
      colours strong rows green and weak rows red, always paired with a
      non-colour glyph tag (never colour-only, repo CVD policy), and rows with
      no matchup verdict stay neutral. The gym renders the identical model.
- [ ] **AC7 — One shared, pure rule.** The selector is pure and Phaser-free,
      lives in the shared core/model (not scene code), is consumed by the game
      and `GymHangar`, and reuses `resolveBossMatchup`, the shipped catalogue
      and the shared slot-cap helper — no second matchup or slot rule.
- [ ] **AC8 — Determinism and idempotence.** The selector is deterministic for
      a given (payload, target, catalogue) — no wall-clock, no unseeded draws —
      and re-applying it does not duplicate entries or oscillate the selection.
- [ ] **AC9 — Automated tests cover every behaviour above**, and the
      changed-scope test gate passes.
- [ ] **AC10 — Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect
      the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or
      docs site entries (GDD § Hangar economy and unlock tree,
      `docs/GYM_PARITY.md`, module JSDoc).
- [ ] **AC11 — Full project test suite.** Full project test suite must pass with
      the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Gym↔game parity (AGENTS.md).** The selection rule must be consumed by the
  game and every gym that renders the hangar screen; `GymHangar` renders the
  same model read-only. No per-scene copy.
- **Reuse the shipped rules.** Matchup verdicts come from
  `resolveBossMatchup`; slot accounting from `POWER_UP_SLOT_CAP` /
  `capDropIdsToSlotPool`; ownership from the pure economy. No new power model.
- **CVD policy.** Colour is never the only signal — the `▲ EFFECTIVE` /
  `▼ RESISTED` glyph tag stays primary.
- **No silent divergence from the six-slot cap.** The selected loadout must
  never present more counted kinds than the run will grant.
- **Determinism.** No wall-clock or unseeded randomness.
- **Scope guard.** Do not re-tune weapon balance, change the matchup resolver,
  or redesign the unlock tree here; those are separate items. Making power-ups
  loadout-selectable is AH-0MWOV8SMI006W52Z, not this item. Do not widen into
  the combat effects of strengths/weaknesses (AH-0MWL5376H001WJFZ).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/core/hangarWar/weaponMatchup.ts` — reuse `resolveBossMatchup` (read-only).
- `src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarScreen.ts` — the model builder, the
  apply-suggested-buildout row/button and the equipped-list rendering.
- `src/core/hangarWar/hangarEconomy.ts` — owned-entry resolution and loadout
  helpers; the new pure selector likely lives in or beside this module.
- `src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarDeployment.ts` — the six-slot grant trim the
  selector must agree with.
- `src/powerups/slots.ts` — `capDropIdsToSlotPool` / `POWER_UP_SLOT_CAP`
  (read-only).
- `src/utils/weapons.ts` — behaviour descriptors (`aoe`, `bounce`, `hitscan`,
  `splits`, `orbit`) the variety rule keys on (read-only).
- `src/scenes/HangarScene.ts` — applies the selection and persists the payload.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymHangar.ts` — read-only parity render.
- `src/scenes/hangarWar/*.test.ts`, `src/core/hangarWar/*.test.ts`,
  `src/scenes/gym/GymHangar.test.ts` — pure-selector and render tests.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — § Hangar economy and unlock tree
  (default-empty wording).
- `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` — parity matrix note.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — the "apply suggested buildout" button clutters the screen.** The
  hangar screen already has DEPLOY / HEX MAP / RESTART rows; mitigation: place
  the new control with the loadout section and keep it in the focus order
  consistently.
- **Risk — empty-loadout detection.** "Default/empty" must mean the shipped
  default (`startingWeapons: []`), not "no strong weapon found". Mitigation:
  auto-fit triggers only when `startingWeapons` is empty; the button covers
  every other case.
- **Risk — power-ups are not selectable yet.** The selector can only budget
  around auto-granted power-ups until AH-0MWOV8SMI006W52Z lands. Mitigation:
  the budget rule is written against the grant list so it becomes selectable
  later without a rewrite.
- **Risk — vague "balanced variety".** Resolved by producer Q3 = A then C; the
  rule keys on shipped behaviour descriptors, not a new taxonomy.
- **Risk — colour-only meaning.** Mitigation: the glyph tag is mandatory (CVD).
- **Risk — scope creep.** Rebalancing weapons, changing the matchup rule, or
  making strengths/weaknesses affect combat are separate items — record as
  linked work, not scope.
- **Assumption A1 — "strong" means `resolveBossMatchup === 'strong'`** (the
  existing display rule, player-centric: a weapon in the boss's `weaknesses`).
- **Assumption A2 — "slots" means the shared six-slot loadout cap.**
- **Assumption A3 — the colouring requirement is shipped for weapon rows**;
  this item preserves it and extends it only where the equipped list is
  changed.
- **Assumption A4 — the automatic selection is a pre-battle default, not a
  mid-run rule**, so it belongs in the hangar model, not the combat core.

## Related work

- AH-0MWOV8SMI006W52Z — Hangar: make owned power-ups installable in the
  deployment loadout (open, discovered-from this item) — the producer's Q2 = A
  follow-on.
- AH-0MWMT4NJV001PX8Y — Weapon-vs-boss matchup resolver (completed) — the
  `strong`/`weak` rule this item reuses.
- AH-0MWMT4QXF0095CBN — Target-aware config screen model and render
  (completed) — the intel block and per-row matchup marking.
- AH-0MWMT4STK001PSK4 — Gym parity and documentation (completed) — the
  gym↔game rendering contract.
- AH-0MWMT4S5U001EGDF — Hex map routes into the config screen (completed) —
  the `targetHexId` path that makes the screen "ahead of a battle".
- AH-0MWOQSV7P002IC5Y — Weak/Resist on hangar equip is misleading (open,
  plan_complete) — sibling: it suppresses the highlight on rows the player
  cannot act on; this item changes *what is selected*, not the highlight
  policy. Not a duplicate.
- AH-0MVVF0POV001JNKX — Loadout can exceed the six-slot cap (completed) — the
  cap and trim rule the selector must honour.
- AH-0MWCFKHWD002RKX9 — Hex War doesn't add initial loadout to slots
  (completed) — deployment → HUD grant path.
- AH-0MWB8VDU4007G1LQ — Model the per-ring deployment loadout (completed) —
  precedent for "equip every owned weapon (slot-capped)" as a modelled loadout;
  this item adds boss-aware selection to that idea.
- AH-0MVZJ6V1J001DA9D — the default-empty loadout decision this item revises.
- AH-0MWL5376H001WJFZ — Make hex strengths and weaknesses matter in combat
  (open) — the mechanical matchup; out of scope here (display-only per
  AH-0MWMT4NJV001PX8Y assumption A7).
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` § Hangar economy and unlock tree.
- `docs/GYM_PARITY.md`.
- `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` Candidate D § Attract mode (auto-select).

## Impact

A player opening the hangar before a hex battle gets a loadout already fitted
to the boss — strong weapons equipped, weak ones left behind, remaining slots
usefully filled — with an explicit button to re-apply the suggestion, so they
can deploy with confidence without re-deriving the intel by hand.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 (RESOLVED) — Trigger and override policy.** When should the automatic
  selection run, and what happens to a hand-picked loadout? Options: A every
  open (persisted); B only when the loadout is default/empty; C behind an
  explicit action; D open but transient.
  - *Answer (producer, 2026-11-20):* **B — auto-fit only when the loadout is at
    its default/empty state — plus provide a button to apply the suggested
    buildout.**
  - *Interpretation:* auto-fit on open when `startingWeapons` is empty, and an
    explicit **apply suggested buildout** button that always renders and applies
    the suggestion on demand. *Source:* interactive reply "1. B (provide a
    button to apply the suggestest buildout)".

- **Q2 (RESOLVED) — Do "power-ups" become loadout-selectable?** Options: A
  budget only; B add power-up selection (large, likely a separate item).
  - *Answer (producer, 2026-11-20):* **A — budget only; create a separate work
    item to add any power-ups that are installable.**
  - *Follow-on:* created **AH-0MWOV8SMI006W52Z — Hangar: make owned power-ups
    installable in the deployment loadout** (feature, discovered-from this
    item). *Source:* interactive reply "2. A - create a separate work item to
    add any power-ups that are installable".

- **Q3 (RESOLVED) — What is "balanced variety"?** Options: A one per behaviour
  family then catalogue order; B round-robin across strong then neutral; C
  prefer strong, then ≥1 defensive power-up, then highest permanent level.
  - *Answer (producer, 2026-11-20):* **A then C.**
  - *Interpretation:* apply the variety cap first (at most one weapon per
    behaviour family), then the preference ordering (strong → at least one
    defensive power-up → highest permanent level) to fill the remaining slots.
    *Source:* interactive reply "3. A then C".

- **Q4 (RESOLVED by repo research) — Does the "colour strong/weak" requirement
  need new work?** The per-row matchup marker (`▲ EFFECTIVE` / `▼ RESISTED`)
  and the strong/weak row colours already ship in `hangarScreen.ts`
  (`withMatchupMarker`, `rowColour`, `HANGAR_STRONG_COLOR` /
  `HANGAR_WEAK_COLOR`). Only weapons carry a boss matchup, so power-up rows are
  neutral. This item preserves that behaviour and covers it with the equipped
  list it changes; no new colour rule is introduced unless the producer asks.
  *Source:* `src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarScreen.ts`,
  `src/core/hangarWar/weaponMatchup.ts`, AH-0MWMT4QXF0095CBN /
  AH-0MWMT4STK001PSK4 (completed).

# Replace in-repo video processing with the `vidc` CLI

**Issue type:** task · **Priority:** high

## User story

As a maintainer, I want AI_Hell to stop owning its own FFmpeg video-processing
pipeline and instead delegate video compilation to the `vidc` CLI
(`video_compiler`), so that video processing has a single maintained home and
this repository contains only game, capture and telemetry code.

## Background

The repository's post-capture video processing lives in the promo compiler:
`scripts/compile-promo.mjs` (FFmpeg argv planning, per-junction
`xfade`/`acrossfade`, VP9/Opus encoding, probe + brightness + pace validation)
plus its pool inventory (`scripts/list-capture-pool.mjs`) and their tests and
docs. `vidc` (cloned at `../video_compiler`) is the replacement engine: it
discovers clips, orders them, probes with `ffprobe`, and renders one normalised
MP4 with a single FFmpeg invocation, supporting formats and render profiles.

Capture (Playwright `MediaRecorder` → WebM), the capture-time probe/seek/remux
helpers and the action-intensity series export are **capture tooling**, not the
post-capture video-processing pipeline, and stay.

## Decisions

- No backward compatibility: the bespoke compiler, its selection/validation
  logic, its manifests and its tests are deleted rather than kept beside vidc.
- Deliverables become MP4 (vidc's native output), replacing the legacy
  VP9/Opus WebM deliverables.
- Missing vidc capabilities surface during this migration are tracked in the
  `video_compiler` project as **high priority** items and synced:
  - `VC-0MWNOFIBI007J8UK` — render integration honours clip bounds
    (`source_range` in/out trimming).
  - `VC-0MWNW4SPX002J2SE` — transition-aware filter graph (per-junction
    `xfade`/`acrossfade`).
  - `VC-0MWNW4SYJ009XMIP` — compile/render transition hand-off.
  (The automated highlight selection is intentionally dropped with the legacy
  pipeline; vidc owns editing.)

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `scripts/compile-promo.mjs` and its type/test files are removed, along
      with `scripts/list-capture-pool.mjs` and its type/test files.
- [ ] A new thin renderer (`scripts/render-promo.mjs`) forwards to
      `vidc render` (binary overridable via `--vidc` / `VIDC_BIN`), forwards
      subprocess output and exit code, supports `--dir`, `--output`,
      `--pattern`, `--format` (repeatable), `--fade-duration`, `--resolution`,
      `--fps`, `--overwrite`, `--dry-run`, `--json` and `--help`.
- [ ] The renderer is covered by unit tests (mocked subprocess) for argv
      forwarding, exit-code propagation, missing-binary remediation and
      `--json`/`--dry-run` passthrough.
- [ ] `package.json` drops the legacy `list:pool` entry and points
      `capture:promo` at the new renderer.
- [ ] The legacy video-processing documentation is removed: the
      "Pool inventory" and "Compiling a promo package" sections of
      `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md`, and the highlight-selection / pace-band
      sections (§7.5, §7.6) of `docs/dev/action-intensity.md`, with
      cross-references and `src/promoCompileDocs.test.ts` updated or removed.
- [ ] Doc guards that imported constants from the deleted compiler
      (`src/actionIntensityDocs.test.ts`, `scripts/promo-scenarios.test.ts`,
      `scripts/capture-scenarios.test.ts`) are updated to use the surviving
      editorial-category vocabulary.
- [ ] `npm run build` and the changed-scope test gate pass.

## Impact

Maintainers no longer carry a bespoke FFmpeg promo pipeline in AI_Hell: video
compilation is delegated to the maintained `vidc` CLI.

## Assumptions

- Capture recording, capture-time probing/remuxing and action-intensity series
  export are capture tooling, not the post-capture video-processing pipeline.
- MP4 is acceptable as the deliverable container for promos.
- Automated highlight selection is out of scope after the migration and is
  removed with the legacy compiler; vidc's timeline editing is the forward path
  once its trimming/transition items land.

## Key Files

- `scripts/compile-promo.mjs`, `scripts/compile-promo.d.mts`
- `scripts/compile-promo.test.ts`, `scripts/compile-promo.e2e.test.ts`
- `scripts/list-capture-pool.mjs`, `scripts/list-capture-pool.d.mts`, `scripts/list-capture-pool.test.ts`
- `scripts/render-promo.mjs`, `scripts/render-promo.d.mts`, `scripts/render-promo.test.ts`
- `package.json`
- `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md`, `docs/dev/action-intensity.md`, `README.md`
- `src/promoCompileDocs.test.ts`, `src/actionIntensityDocs.test.ts`
- `scripts/promo-scenarios.mjs`, `scripts/promo-scenarios.test.ts`
- `scripts/capture-scenarios.mjs`, `scripts/capture-scenarios.test.ts`, `scripts/capture-scenario-schema.mjs`

# Hangar: make owned power-ups installable in the deployment loadout

## Problem statement

Today every owned level-bearing power-up is granted automatically on deployment (`buildHangarDeployment` carries `levels.powerUps`, and `applyHangarWarDeployment` grants them) and is **not** part of `HangarLoadout`, which has only `startingWeapons` and `modifiers`. The hangar screen therefore has no way to choose *which* power-ups a deployment installs — the player can only buy/upgrade them, and the auto-loadout selector can only budget around them.

## User story

*As a player,* I want to choose which owned power-ups my deployment installs, so I can curate a build for the upcoming hex rather than carrying every owned power-up and having the six-slot cap trim the rest.

## Desired change

- Extend the loadout model (additively, no schema bump) so a deployment can select a subset of owned, level-bearing power-ups.
- Render owned power-ups as toggleable rows in the hangar deployment selector (alongside starting weapons and modifiers), respecting `POWER_UP_SLOT_CAP` shared with weapons.
- Resolve and grant exactly the selected power-ups in `buildHangarDeployment` / `applyHangarWarDeployment`; keep an empty selection legal and preserve the current default behaviour for saves without the new field.
- Feed the selection into the auto-loadout selector (parent AH-0MWOROJYT004WPSD) so its "balanced variety" can include chosen power-ups.
- Keep gym↔game parity: `GymHangar` renders the same model read-only.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Owned level-bearing power-ups appear as toggleable rows in the hangar deployment selector, with a clear equipped/unequipped state.
- [ ] A deployment grants exactly the selected power-ups (and their permanent levels); deselected power-ups are not granted.
- [ ] The combined selected weapons + power-ups respect the shared six-slot cap, and the displayed loadout matches what the run grants.
- [ ] A save written before this feature (no selection field) deploys with the existing behaviour, with no schema bump.
- [ ] The auto-loadout selector can select power-ups once this lands.
- [ ] The game and `GymHangar` render from the same model.
- [ ] Automated tests cover the model, the resolve/grant path and the gym parity.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated (GDD, `docs/GYM_PARITY.md`, JSDoc).
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass.

## Constraints

- Reuse the shipped slot cap and grant seams; no second power-up budget.
- Additive persisted field only (same pattern as `weaponLevels` / `powerUpLevels`).
- Do not change power-up balance or the six-slot semantics.

## Related work

- AH-0MWOROJYT004WPSD — Automatically select strong weapons (parent; producer Q2 = A, this item spawned for installable power-ups).
- AH-0MVVF0POV001JNKX — Loadout can exceed the six-slot cap.
- AH-0MWCFKHWD002RKX9 — Hex War doesn't add initial loadout to slots.
- AH-0MVZJ6V1J001DA9D — default-empty loadout decision.

## Impact

Players can curate which owned power-ups a deployment installs, so the loadout they see is the loadout they fly.
